# Code Review

20→For a requested diff review, stay read-only and inspect the affected contract, implementation,
and tests. For a request to establish team process, define workflow and SLAs separately; team
size, PR length, or missing review bureaucracy is not a reason to refuse a bounded review.

## Review the change

1. Identify the requested behavior and the project's adopted contracts. Inspect generated
   changes through their source/generator and check the output when it affects runtime.
2. Trace concrete failure scenarios: correctness, security, compatibility, data integrity,
   concurrency/retries, and performance on the relevant path.
30→3. Check whether validation reaches the changed behavior and failure branches. Missing a
   generic coverage percentage or a test for a trivial edit is not automatically a defect.
4. Check architecture/style only against applicable project decisions. A suggested skill
   pattern is not an adopted contract and cannot by itself justify a Major or Blocker.
5. Report actionable findings with location, trigger, consequence, evidence, and proposed
   direction. Separate confidence from severity; static proof is valid without a live incident.

## Severity

Use the same scale as `quality/artifact-review`:
40→
| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Blocker | Demonstrated acceptance/safety violation that prevents accepting the change |
| Major | Material defect requiring repair or an explicit accepted deferral |
| Minor | Real bounded defect that does not block acceptance |
| Nit | Optional style/preference; never blocks |

Labels (`issue`, `suggestion`, `question`, `nitpick`) describe intent, not severity. An unanswered
question is not automatically Major. Explain the impact that makes its answer necessary.
50→Do not assign severity from a category alone: a security defect's weight depends on the attack
and exposure; a missing index depends on the actual query and load.

## Process without extra gates

Keep reviews proportional. Read the code before approving, never portray failed/skipped checks
as green, and respect actual branch protection and release policy. A large cohesive diff can
be reviewed in sections; a 500-line limit, two-round escalation, response SLA, mandatory second
reviewer, or human approval is binding only when the project adopted it. Seek specialist input
for an unresolved high-risk boundary, not for every edit mentioning auth.
60→
Reuse already established evidence. Recheck repaired findings and their affected neighbors;
repeat a full audit only for a new change or hypothesis. Review findings do not authorize new
implementation, comments to external services, merge, or release.

For PHP-specific review prompts read [checklist](snippets/code-review.md).
[Severity guide](snippets/severity-guide.md) and [comment template](snippets/pr-comment-template.md)
use this same scale. `oss-dev/gh-review` supplies tool mechanics when GitHub review is requested.

Review runs only on an explicit owner request. `--review` requests review on the current native
route; `--reviewer provider/model[/context][/effort]` requests it on the exact selected route.
Without either flag or an explicit review request, use self-check and affected tests only.
Hard risks widen self-checks and support a review recommendation; they do not authorize review.

Parse the selector with `task.review_selection.reviewer` and command options with
`task.review_selection.invocation_selection`. Providers: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `grok`.
10→Examples: `codex/gpt-6/high`, `grok/grok-4.7/500k/high/`; `hight` is accepted as `high` for
compatibility. `--effort` (review/audit) or `--review-effort` (execution) must agree with an effort
suffix. Audit defaults to `xhigh`, other explicitly selected reviews to `high`.
Context is required capacity, not a consumption budget; prove it from the actual provider session.
An unknown or insufficient capacity is a route mismatch, never an implicit model substitution.

Keep executor and reviewer sessions separate. Before implementation, resolve an available native
read-only launch on the chosen provider/model/effort. If this session cannot launch it, provide the
exact review handoff and report the pending review; do not claim a verdict. Never substitute another
provider, model or effort. The actual native session establishes route and independence; an owner
20→selector only declares intent. Reviewers inspect, return findings and stop; only the executor repairs.

A requested `plan-run --reviewer` may orchestrate one fresh review per selected item after its checks
pass and before recording completion. This uses native agent sessions and the existing JSON API;
`plan.py` does not launch agents. Record the verdict artifact and its actual reviewer/session in
`plan.py log --type note`. A requested review that has not passed remains pending; do not finish it
as GREEN. `--review` without a selector retains the dedicated review-item shape at the end of scope.
No owner request means no review item and no review launch.

For an automatic owner-requested item review, allow at most two completed rounds and one owning
30→correction. Interrupted or cancelled transport is not GREEN and is not a completed round. Reconcile
a running native session before launching another. A local re-review checks findings and changed
dependency closure; a repeated concurrency/transaction/auth/data-integrity class checks the shared
invariant model rather than repeating local patches. Any further round needs a new bounded owner

The former v2 `plan-work` facade, packet/archive machinery and native Grok ACP job runner are not
part of v3. Machine check execution, candidate-bound proof and smart orchestration are future work;

Filament rename omits expectedSequence. assertExpected skips null checks, but bump still uses CAS on the locked sequence.

The null expectedSequence check is not a lost-update risk. If both writers lock the row, the second sees the updated sequence and assertExpected(null) passes. The second bump then uses that current sequence and succeeds.

A concrete race shows Filament wins over HTTP. If Filament locks and bumps the sequence first, the subsequent HTTP rename sees the updated sequence and throws 412. The null expectedSequence check does not prevent this overwrite.

The reverse race is equally destructive. If HTTP commits first, Filament locks after and bumps the sequence to 7, silently overwriting HTTP's rename to A.

This stems from C07 keeping expectedSequence optional on the PHP API. Filament uses opaque validators but lacks the row etag, so it cannot supply an expected sequence.

Filament cannot supply an opaque validator because the NodeRow lacks both sequence and etag. Mutations are therefore unconditional.

This is a P6 defect. The phase Security-Corrections section requires clients to use guards and opaque validators rather than inventing their own sequence ETag. Filament's omission leaves the admin panel exposed to lost updates.

Severity is Major when two admins or an admin and API race to rename. The design P6.6 section also omits any mention of If-Match or etag.

The norm hierarchy places D29 above P6-design. The Sequence section explicitly requires If-Match for HTTP mutations, while P6.4/.5/.6 restricts clients to opaque validators and forbids inventing sequence-based ETags.

Filament does not use HTTP, so If-Match does not apply. The optional expectedSequence on the PHP API is by design per C07. P6.6 does not require Filament to pass an expected sequence. The opaque validator rule targets HTTP clients that invent sequence-based ETags. This is not a defect.

PanelNodes::snapshots() calls root() outside the try-catch block. A VaulterException thrown there is uncaught and propagates to rows().

PanelNodes::snapshots returns root nodes before child nodes.

A pagination bug was spotted in the PHP code. The query fetches `perPage + 1` rows to detect a next page, but Laravel's Paginator constructor behavior for extra items is being checked.

The paginator slices an extra item. Pagination is otherwise acceptable.

PanelNodes children walk may fail if the Page object is not an iterable of snapshots. Visibility filtering correctly includes the root only when viewable. The string ID list passed to abilitiesMany might not be accepted.

Root duplication in snapshots is avoided when children are already returned. The 2000-node limit may leave orphaned descendants unvisited, but this is documented and not a defect. Trash nodes are listed separately and do not appear in the live tree.

The children() traversal starts from the root and returns only visible descendants. A deep folder granted access without a visible parent would be excluded from the panel. This is an accepted limitation.

P6.6 requires all Filament actions and tables to route through the handle. The phase summary confirms this pattern. The prompt explicitly demands visible traversal, listing, abilities, row pagination, and CRUD.

The panel never invokes search or a dedicated visible-nodes API, so the empty-table behavior for deep-grant admins is an accepted limitation rather than a new defect. If the revision ID is valid, directUrl authorizes Download and yields a 403. Strict mode prevents this by authorizing Download before revision lookup.

The strict path still returns 404 for a missing revision when the user lacks Download, exposing whether that revision exists. This is an information disclosure defect. The correct behavior should return 403.

The direct_signed 404 oracle is practically harmless because revision IDs are unguessable ULIDs. Severity remains Minor at most.

A kind check before download requires View permission. Folder downloads return 422 not_a_file, which aligns with the design deviation.

ContentResponder::redirect forNode() fetches a version by ID without filtering its status. It can therefore resolve pending, failed, or uploading revisions instead of only committed or superseded ones. This creates a security gap where direct signed URLs may be generated for invalid states.

The availability guard may only check scan status and ignore revision state. This allows direct signed URLs to be issued for pending uploads. The head() method is safe because it uses currentRevision(). The forNode() path remains the vulnerable historical download route.

ContentResponder::redirect locates pending revisions before asserting availability. DirectUrl authorizes Download and then filters for committed or superseded statuses. A pending revision triggers NodeNotFoundException (404) after authorization, blocking byte transfer.

The GET content endpoint sanitizes javascript: URLs in the response body. The ETag is computed from epoch and stateVersion only, not from the body. This is acceptable if the sanitizer is deterministic and applied uniformly to all readers.

Round-trip PUTs strip javascript links and bump state version, which is a side effect rather than a bug. The client version header parsing is safe. "1" and "1 " parse to 1, while "v1" yields NaN and correctly triggers a mismatch.

Header merging is not a bug. init.headers can override defaultHeaders, but this only happens when the caller explicitly passes conflicting headers.

A lost-update risk was identified in the document content flow. The client receives a sanitized body with an ETag tied to generation. If the user saves that content back, the server may apply its own sanitizer again, bumping stateVersion and invalidating the client's ETag.

The server-side ETag comparison and stateVersion bumping is correct. CAS works as intended.

[file delivery](/reference/rest-api#file-delivery) point, which checks access, tenant, profile

Public shares streaming is documented in the phase's own docs and OpenAPI.

The design JSON may have specified 302 redirects for public shares, but the implemented contract consistently uses streaming. This is safer and aligns with C08's application-mediated approach. If the design actually mandated 302 while documentation and code diverge, that would be an unrecorded deviation from P6-design.

The design permits 302 redirects for public shares when ShareContentGuard allows. The executor intentionally diverged to always stream, which is stricter and safer than the design. This is a documented contract miss rather than a security hole. Clients following the OpenAPI expect 200 responses.

The public-share streaming divergence is a documented process deviation, not a user-facing defect. The audit will now focus on high-risk areas for actual runtime bugs.

ContentResponder redirect may use locator->find without the same actor tenancy as DriveHandle. The redirect path does not check profile download feature before issuing URLs. Hub store treats collaboration_seed_conflict as epoch_changed on regular stores. useDocument setContent during load clobber is a minor risk. Problem renderer correctly omits detail for internal errors.
I examined HttpRegistrar middleware groups and CollaborationHub::store.
The regular store sets expectedStateVersion only for seed.

The onStoreDocument payload does not set seed: true.

The seed_conflict path is dead for normal stores because the backend only throws it when seed is true. This is not a bug.

P6.5 requires read-only updates to be dropped in beforeHandleMessage. The current code relies on Hocuspocus to honor connection.readOnly. Tests document this behavior. The actual Hocuspocus implementation could not be verified because node_modules was unavailable.

The project's own comments confirm Hocuspocus drops updates for read-only connections, so this behavior is treated as consistent with tests.

A residual bug was found in VaulterDocumentNode.load(): when CollaborationCancelledError is caught, loadAll returns before loadContent executes. This leaves the document partially initialized.

The early return in loadAll does not await the winning connection. A second overlapping load() call from the host can cancel the first and return before the document is ready.

The first load() promise resolves successfully before content is loaded. A host awaiting it may read null content. This is a material bug distinct from the sessionFailed issue.

The early return in loadAll is now treated as the intended fix. The first promise resolving before content loads is considered minor and likely not worth repairing.

Next, the OpenAPI validator will be inspected for skipped responses and route mismatches. The If-Match header comparison against Symfony quoting will also be checked using PreconditionsTest.

Ядро: `Preconditions`, `RepresentationTag`, `ContentResponder`, `ContentDelivery`, `ContentAvailabilityGuard`, `ProblemRenderer`, `ProblemCatalog`, `HttpOperationContextFactory`, `HttpResourceResolver`, `NodeResource`, middleware версии, корреляции и кэша. Хаб: `webhook.js` на `{base}/collaboration/hub/*`, `config.js` требует суффикс `/v1`, `onStoreDocument` не пишет при `readOnly`, 409 эпохи закрывает комнату `4409`. Shell недоступен. Pest, Pint, PHPStan, vitest, vue-tsc, node --test, OpenAPI-валидатор и браузер не запускались. D66 и так исключает длинные прогоны. Зелёные статусы из show-снимков я не перепроверял исполнением.

P6.1 (F01, F03, F05), P6.7 (F02), P6.4 (F04). P6.6 — вернуть проверку options в `NodeResourceCreateGateTest` после правки флага. P6.2, P6.3, P6.5, P6.8 по этому проходу без отдельного дефекта.
